messages.subject: Error when running ectotherm model ("Error in ectout$yearsout")
messages.subject_clean: Error when running ectotherm model ("Error in ectout$yearsout")
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I've run into an issue with the ectotherm model. I understand that the ecotherm model hasn't been officially released yet but I was hoping someone may be able to help.

I've run the micro climate model over a 5-year period:
micro<-micro_global(loc = "Townsville, Queensland", nyears = 5)

I've then attempted to run the ectotherm model (default settings) with the following code:
ecto<-ectotherm(nyears = micro$nyears)

When I run this, I get the following error:
running ectotherm model ...
   user  system elapsed
   0.45    0.00    0.47
Error in ectout$yearsout[1:nyears, ] : subscript out of bounds

This error only occurs when nyears >1. Is it logical to run the micro climate for 5 years (or any number of years for that matter) and then run the ectotherm model?

I have read the available documentation but have been unable to troubleshoot this issue on my own.

Any assistance would be appreciated.

messages.subject_clean: Error when running ectotherm model ("Error in ectout$yearsout")
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

Thanks for pointing out the problem. You are running the microclimate model for 5 years but for the middle day of each month. If you use 'timeinterval = 365' in the call to the microclimate model you'll get results splined for 365 days of each year and then the ectotherm model will run fine. In the near future I'll fix the bug you found so it will work for other values of 'timeinterval'.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: get.global.climate() layers
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Is there a list/documentation detailing what the 97 different layers correspond to when downloading the global climate data using:

get.global.climate()

>From what I can see, the original CRU dataset has substantially fewer layers than 97. CRU v1 has 11 layers (https://crudata.uea.ac.uk/~timm/grid/CRU_CL_1_0.html) and CRU v2 has 8 layers. Even when adding cloud cover and aerosol layers, I can't work out how this totals 97.

Many thanks,

Simon

messages.subject: Re: get.global.climate() layers
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

They are per month. If you look in the code for the micro_global function you'll see what's pasted below which should tell you what you need to know (ALTT is elevation). The function 'build_global_climate' creates it from scratch. I'll add some documentation to the package so it's a bit more obvious (and note the divisions by 10 to get the values into the right units - they are stored in integer form in the data set to keep the file size down).

All the best,
Mike

        global_climate <- raster::brick(paste(folder, "/global_climate.nc <http://global_climate.nc>",
            sep = ""))
        CLIMATE <- raster::extract(global_climate, x)
        ALTT <- as.numeric(CLIMATE[, 1])
        RAINFALL <- CLIMATE[, 2:13]
        RAINYDAYS <- CLIMATE[, 14:25]/10
        WNMAXX <- CLIMATE[, 26:37]/10
        WNMINN <- WNMAXX * 0.1
        TMINN <- CLIMATE[, 38:49]/10
        TMAXX <- CLIMATE[, 50:61]/10
        ALLMINTEMPS <- TMINN
        ALLMAXTEMPS <- TMAXX
        ALLTEMPS <- cbind(ALLMAXTEMPS, ALLMINTEMPS)
        RHMINN <- CLIMATE[, 62:73]/10
        RHMAXX <- CLIMATE[, 74:85]/10
        CCMINN <- CLIMATE[, 86:97]/10
